STANDERTON SHAMBLES

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Lekwa Municipality is broken on every level. We investigate ineffective service delivery and corruption at the hands of those in charge.

Summary:
It’s the story of almost every single small town around the country - no water, no electricity, raw sewage in the streets and no basic services for months on end. In Standerton, Mpumalanga, the municipal workers have also had enough - tools down - and protesting against the municipal manager with a chequered past, who’s done nothing to fix this destitute town. Simply put, on every level, Standerton is an epic failure of accountability.


Further information:
ISSUES
- ELECTRICITY – the municipality owes over R1 Billion, permanent loadshedding – off for 24 hours when usage went over 55mkv during protests
- WATER – severely polluted – 1000 units per 100 ml of water is the acceptable standard. In June 2019 it was just over a R1million. In May 2020 – a staggering 2,4 million 2 /3 pump stations are working
- SEWAGE – not working….From 2011 R100 millioin was spent to fiz water sewarge treatment works - Ludonga Contractors, Kipp Consulting Engineers, Nathoo Mbenyane Engineers, Tsa Legae Trading and VDan Construction. 6 out of 11 working
- FIRE DEPARTMENT – not functioning – October 2019 – three children under the age of 12 burnt to death.
- CORRUPTION - R1,7billion of which R1.1billion was owed to Eskom
EXTRACT AUDITOR GENERAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT AUDIT – MFMA 2018-2019
Lekwa (MP) – R47 million: All tender documents were kept in the municipal manager’s office and could not be submitted for audit purposes within the agreed turnaround time. These submission challenges persisted even after discussions with the municipal manager in audit steering committee meetings, in which she committed that officials must retrieve and submit the requested tender documents to her office. Some tender documents were subsequently submitted, but these could not be audited because they did not contain all the required information such as scoring sheets and advertisements.

CURRENT STATE OF AFFAIRS – JUNE 2020 A46 FOURTH QUARTER FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE REPORT TO LEKWA COUNCIL
The creditors age analysis indicates an analysis of unpaid received invoices, aged by due date. The creditors are broken down into four ageing periods.

The Creditors Age Analysis shows an outstanding amount of R1,7billion of which R1.1billion was owed to Eskom. The municipality has taken several initiatives to ensure that the arrears amount owed to Eskom is paid. The Department of Community Safety, Security and Liaison has an outstanding amount of R85million. The latest outstanding amount for Department of Water and Sanitation is R421million. There is a contingency provision for an amount of R332 million owed to the Department of Water Affairs and Sanitation that is under dispute.
The Municipality has had numerous engagements with the Department of Water & Sanitation during the month of March 2015, where the Department has conceded that they have incorrectly billed the Municipality since 2015. The Department has committed to correcting the account and passing the necessary correcting adjustments. This will significantly reduce the outstanding debts.
The Municipality’s outstanding trade creditors amounts to R1.9million. The Municipality owes the Auditor General an amount of R4.1million. The Municipality withheld retention amounting to R8.8 million.
The Municipality owes SARS an amount of R81million of which R57million is in relation to PAYE and R24million in relation to VAT. The Municipality does not maintain sufficient working capital thus resulting in statutory payments and some other creditors not being paid timeously. The outstanding creditors are continuously increasing thus indicating that the Municipality is entering into obligations that is unable to service. Unless all interventions are implemented (Revenue enhancement strategy, financial recovery, cost curtailments & installation of smart meters) the Municipality will face a severe financial sustainability issues & distress, that might require the Municipality to consider interventions as entrenched within the Municipal Finance Management Act.

ACTION TAKEN
- The municipality appeared before the Cooperative Governance and traditional Affairs Committee in Parliament on December 3
o MM Gugu Mhlongo Ntshangase – said they approached treasury for assistance – and it had committed to provide Lekwa with two trucks – but Treasury not aware of this.
- Department of Water and Sanitation – issued notice and directive in terms of national water act – act 36 of 1998, section (3) and 53 (1) – I addition applied for an urgent court interdict to force municipality to comply with directive – granted 18 sept 2018.
- Special Forensic Report commissioned by COGTA Mpumalanga in July 2018 – not favourable
- Human Right Commission Report

MUNICIPAL MANAGER TRACK RECORD
- Ms Ntshangase left Utrecht Municipality under a cloud of corruption – she was charged under Prevention and Combating of Corrupt Activities Act 12 of 2004 (PCCA) regarding her conduct as the Municipal Manger of Emadlangeni Municipality – Utrecht CAS 36/09/2017 – despite overwhelming evidence against Ms Ntshangase no prosecution was instituted.

This stems from a 148 page report on Investigation into Allegations of Misconduct Pertaining to Municipal Manager Gugu Petunia Ntshangase dated 25 October 2016 done by GL Seethal on behalf of Seethal Attorneys – the investigation arises out of an instruction received from the Emadlangeni Municipality in Utrecht.

Issues around tender awards and personal security – which has cropped up in Standerton as well.


CHARACTERS
• Gary van Aswegen – RATE PAYERS ASSOCIATION (will speak to impact on businesses – I am busy doing a survey with farmers and big businesses in the area)
• Pheelo – INFORMAL COMMUNITY REPRESENTATIVE
• Louis van Rensburg – OPPOSITION PARTY (BACKGROUND AND CONTEXT TO GUGU’S REIGN, ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT)
• Sifiso – SAMWU – STRIKING WORKER VOICE
• Lekwa Municipality – MM Gugu Nsthangase
• William Gumede – Independent Voice on Local Government & corruption.


WHAT WE’LL SHOW
- BROKEN SEWAGE PLANTS
- BROKEN WATER PUMP STATIONS
- POLLUTION
- IMPACTED COMMUNITIES WITH SEWAGE JUST ABOUT IN THEIR HOMES
- PROTESTING MUNICIPAL WORKERS
- POTHOLES AND NEGLECTED STREET SCENES
- AN EMPTY MUNICIPALITY – ABANDONED SINCE THE PROTESTS

STRUCTURE

VO: The people of Standerton have had enough. Constant power outages, polluted water and raw sewage in the streets have become a daily reality in Lekwa (local) Municipality.

LINK: This is what residents of standerton had to resort to dumping their rubbish right at the door of the municipality to try and get the attention. When you have ineffective service delivery. This. Is what happens

VO: In July this year, a 2018 Forensic Report was finally tabled at a Municipal Council Meeting. Local Councillor for an opposition party, Louis Jansen van Rensburg, says the findings were damning.

LOUIS: the municipal manager. It seems like it's alleged that she's saying she's got dirty fingers //

VO: Ranging from mismanagement to irregular payments to questionable service provider appointments - the long list of issues has resulted in ineffective service delivery and a breakdown within the oraganisation.

LINK: In the Lekwa Municipality in Mpumalanga – the town of Standerton is broken and the stench of corruption and mismanagement is overwhelming.

VO: On the 3rd of August Lekwa Municipal Workers downed tools and started daily protests - burning tyres and rubbish fill the air with smoke - even the workers have had enough.

SIFISO: This is not going to end anytime soon. If this municipal manager is not gone it's not going to end

VO: The Municipal Manager is Gugu Mhlongo-Ntshangase.

Sifiso Zacarais from the South African Municipal Workers Union, says besides COVID19 labour remuneration issues and PPE shortages - they won’t stand for corruption.

SIFISO: The status of this municipalities upside down. And I would say this without any fear. Regional the leadership of the ANC knows about this.

VO: The Municipality currently owes creditors 1.7 billion Rands. Of that amount, R1.1 billion is owed to Eskom. This has led to daily electricity throttling, explains Wilma Venter from the Lekwa Ratepayers Association.

WILMA: This is not the normal load shedding that Eskom implements. This is purely due to non-payment that we as a town are experiencing these power cuts

VO: With regular power cuts the water purification plant can't run at full capacity impacting on water supply. But the bigger issue, is the procurement of chemicals needed to treat the water, according to plant Supervisor - Vusi Hlatshwayo.

VUSI WATER: we are extracting our raw water from the river. And then it means that that water is full of water borne disease. So if you don't have an enough chemical or the right chemical to purify the water then you will you will actually kill all the community.

VO: In March - the Purification Plant ran out of chemicals, despite numerous requests for new stock. Hlatshwayo and his team made a difficult decision to switch off the plant - cutting the town’s water supply.

VUSI WATER: The M M arrested that myself I am supervisor, arrested even the manager. He arrested even the HOD. We don't have the authority to switch off the plant without his knowledge. But according to us we did the write a lot of reports.

VO: The charges were later withdrawn, but the water quality issues have yet to be resolved.

Drinking water samples taken by the Department of Water and Sanitation in March, confirmed contamination.

LINK: This is the everyday reality of the people of Sakhile raw sewage coming from a manhole that spews down the street and cascades all the way right through the township.

VO: Community Member Pheello Mlotswa says residents regularly have sewage flowing through their properties.

PHEELLO: This is where all the mess is coming from. They have to dig a trench to let it roll out straight
MAC: and this is 24 hours every day
PHEELLO: every day 24 houra
MAC: So what people what are people saying about this.
PHEELLO: people have complained and I think they're tired of complaining cos nothing happens. So they have to stay like this they have to accept what's going on.
MAC: You know this is this is unacceptable. Are you hearing of people getting sick or getting illnesses from this is.
PHEELLO: Yes, And most of the people living around here are people who are pensioners // And they are getting sick every day
MAC: Sjoh

VO: It’s a problem all around the town with raw sewage water overflowing in the streets and into the river.

LINK: This is one of 11 pump stations around the town of Standerton and as you can see it's not pumping much. It's right next to a residential area. And it stinks.

VO: While the municipality has spent over R100 million on sewage works repairs in the last decade, many of the pump stations are not operational. Andrew Uys lives next door to one.

ANDREW: It's on and off. Sometimes it works a little bit. They come and do something it works a bit and then it just stops working.

VO: There’s been a spike in properties for sale, and business and farming operations are starting to buckle under the pressure of constant service interruptions.

The Rate Payers Association legally challenged Eskom’s electricity throttling, and were granted a court interdict, prohibiting additional future load reduction.

While Lekwa Municipality Mayor Linda Dhlamini, sympathises with residents - he explains that the municipality is battling to balance aging infrastructure and budgets.

MAYOR: challenges...

VO: As Mayor he is politically appointed and not the accounting officer - this would be Mhlongo-Ntshangase.

Lekwa is not her first shot at being a Municipal Manager. She left Emadlangeni Municipality in KZN under a cloud of corruption in 2017.

We spoke to an ANC councillor based there, on condition of anonymity.

ANC MAN: there was an independent investigation that was initiated by the Council and after having received a number of allegations related to her conduct in respect of management as well as some of the decisions that she had taken which was m payments just to have irregular payments to service providers irregular appointments of staff. //. Appointment of security companies without following due process.

UPSOUND CALL
LINK: She doesn’t answer our calls, she doesn’t get back to us, we’ve heard that she’s inside maybe she’ll speak to us in person.

LINK: so we jsut saw GN get in the car // she simply ignores us - she’s surrounded by security.

MAC: Hi, can we speak to GN - she’s not any of these cars?

VO: Mhlongo-Ntshangase travels with bodyguards, who are also stationed outside her office every day.

SIFISO: The army of the municipal manager. 1 2 3 4 //that are paid by us that are paid by us taxpayers money.
LOUIS: they get paid about 70 to 80 to 90 thousand grand a month. We didn't have a clue where that come from. It's not being discussed in council.// but they are costing us millions

VO: Mhlongo-Ntshangase hasn’t responded to our emails or whatsapps. Zacarias says this is her modus operandi.

SIFISO: From day one she never wanted to account// we’ve made arrangement to have meetings with her - she’ll just disown them.

VO: Zacarias took us into the Municipal Building - the council chambers have been renovated to meet COVID19 regulations. The installation is basic with some plug points fitted incorrectly. According to SAMWU - it came at a price tag of R1.5 million.

MAC: Even if Labor included this cannot honestly cost one and a half million rand
SIFISO: 33 in total
MAC: 33 of these
SIFISO Even if each was ten thousand rands it wouldn't have made including his deletion does it needs a genius rocket scientist to fit this thing here?

VO: Questionable Expenditure is not unusual at Lekwa Municipality - the Auditor General was unable to audit R47 million’s worth of procurement in the 2018-2019 Local Government report.

SIFISO: If you are going to have a municipal manager that is going to Keep or look tender documents in the office and should and wanted to submit them for auditing and all of that. What does that tells you.

LINK: Over the last two years there has been intervention from the Department of Water and Sanitation the Human Rights Commission and even COGTA yet not much has changed at Lekwa municipality. 00:01:29:13 - 00:01:39:14

VO: There is talk of the municipality going under administration - but the process has not commenced yet.

LOUIS: You feel like you report it's like the snake to Satan if you take it up with a COGTA You see how the things are run in SA, so that you can you know there's no political will to rectify anything in any small town in Mpumalanga M29

GUMEDE: This is not not an exception. This is the story. Of municipal governments across the country

VO: Professor William Gumede is chairmain of the Democracy Works Foundation.

GUMEDE: Really it is a crisis. I think the very first. Thing that we have to look at it is a lack of political will. Swear to hold people accountable. M2

VO: But Mayor Dlamini is adamant that the council is aware of the irregularities and insists that it will be investigated.

MAYOR: the institution is seriously under strain. Accountablitiy is not a choice - it must happen in even Lekwa….accountablity - there are challenges that are evident - we must not hide them - we must confront them and deal with them decisively //

VO: BUt there were no consequences for Mhlongo-Ntshangase at her previous post - despite a 148 page independent report commissioned by the municipality. Nothing came of the Internal disciplinary processes or criminal charges that were brought against her.

MAC How does someone like this get away with this. You know this. This is an epic failure of accountability and acting with total impunity.
ANC MAN: you cannot dodge so many bullets unless you are being shielded from the powers that be. That would be my assumption.

GUMEDE: the same people who are politically connected and recycled over and over even if they've been involved in wrongdoing // because you know they are really the protectors Of. tender this to the protectors of you know Jobs for palls .
LOUIS: The infighting in the in the system. It's us as a municipal ratepayers. We are the ones that get the bitter end of it.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Lekwa Municipality is broken on every level. We investigate ineffective service delivery and corruption at the hands of those in charge.
metadata.Summary: It’s the story of almost every single small town around the country - no water, no electricity, raw sewage in the streets and no basic services for months on end. In Standerton, Mpumalanga, the municipal workers have also had enough - tools down - and protesting against the municipal manager with a chequered past, who’s done nothing to fix this destitute town. Simply put, on every level, Standerton is an epic failure of accountability.
metadata.Further information: ISSUES - ELECTRICITY – the municipality owes over R1 Billion, permanent loadshedding – off for 24 hours when usage went over 55mkv during protests - WATER – severely polluted – 1000 units per 100 ml of water is the acceptable standard. In June 2019 it was just over a R1million. In May 2020 – a staggering 2,4 million 2 /3 pump stations are working - SEWAGE – not working….From 2011 R100 millioin was spent to fiz water sewarge treatment works - Ludonga Contractors, Kipp Consulting Engineers, Nathoo Mbenyane Engineers, Tsa Legae Trading and VDan Construction. 6 out of 11 working - FIRE DEPARTMENT – not functioning – October 2019 – three children under the age of 12 burnt to death. - CORRUPTION - R1,7billion of which R1.1billion was owed to Eskom EXTRACT AUDITOR GENERAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT AUDIT – MFMA 2018-2019 Lekwa (MP) – R47 million: All tender documents were kept in the municipal manager’s office and could not be submitted for audit purposes within the agreed turnaround time. These submission challenges persisted even after discussions with the municipal manager in audit steering committee meetings, in which she committed that officials must retrieve and submit the requested tender documents to her office. Some tender documents were subsequently submitted, but these could not be audited because they did not contain all the required information such as scoring sheets and advertisements. CURRENT STATE OF AFFAIRS – JUNE 2020 A46 FOURTH QUARTER FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE REPORT TO LEKWA COUNCIL The creditors age analysis indicates an analysis of unpaid received invoices, aged by due date. The creditors are broken down into four ageing periods. The Creditors Age Analysis shows an outstanding amount of R1,7billion of which R1.1billion was owed to Eskom. The municipality has taken several initiatives to ensure that the arrears amount owed to Eskom is paid. The Department of Community Safety, Security and Liaison has an outstanding amount of R85million. The latest outstanding amount for Department of Water and Sanitation is R421million. There is a contingency provision for an amount of R332 million owed to the Department of Water Affairs and Sanitation that is under dispute. The Municipality has had numerous engagements with the Department of Water & Sanitation during the month of March 2015, where the Department has conceded that they have incorrectly billed the Municipality since 2015. The Department has committed to correcting the account and passing the necessary correcting adjustments. This will significantly reduce the outstanding debts. The Municipality’s outstanding trade creditors amounts to R1.9million. The Municipality owes the Auditor General an amount of R4.1million. The Municipality withheld retention amounting to R8.8 million. The Municipality owes SARS an amount of R81million of which R57million is in relation to PAYE and R24million in relation to VAT. The Municipality does not maintain sufficient working capital thus resulting in statutory payments and some other creditors not being paid timeously. The outstanding creditors are continuously increasing thus indicating that the Municipality is entering into obligations that is unable to service. Unless all interventions are implemented (Revenue enhancement strategy, financial recovery, cost curtailments & installation of smart meters) the Municipality will face a severe financial sustainability issues & distress, that might require the Municipality to consider interventions as entrenched within the Municipal Finance Management Act. ACTION TAKEN - The municipality appeared before the Cooperative Governance and traditional Affairs Committee in Parliament on December 3 o MM Gugu Mhlongo Ntshangase – said they approached treasury for assistance – and it had committed to provide Lekwa with two trucks – but Treasury not aware of this. - Department of Water and Sanitation – issued notice and directive in terms of national water act – act 36 of 1998, section (3) and 53 (1) – I addition applied for an urgent court interdict to force municipality to comply with directive – granted 18 sept 2018. - Special Forensic Report commissioned by COGTA Mpumalanga in July 2018 – not favourable - Human Right Commission Report MUNICIPAL MANAGER TRACK RECORD - Ms Ntshangase left Utrecht Municipality under a cloud of corruption – she was charged under Prevention and Combating of Corrupt Activities Act 12 of 2004 (PCCA) regarding her conduct as the Municipal Manger of Emadlangeni Municipality – Utrecht CAS 36/09/2017 – despite overwhelming evidence against Ms Ntshangase no prosecution was instituted. This stems from a 148 page report on Investigation into Allegations of Misconduct Pertaining to Municipal Manager Gugu Petunia Ntshangase dated 25 October 2016 done by GL Seethal on behalf of Seethal Attorneys – the investigation arises out of an instruction received from the Emadlangeni Municipality in Utrecht. Issues around tender awards and personal security – which has cropped up in Standerton as well.
